frontMatter.introduction:
At Arminak Solutions LLC dba KBL Cosmetics, we are committed to delivering high-quality, innovative, and sustainable cosmetic manufacturing solutions. Our turnkey, private label, and contract manufacturing services are backed by strict adherence to quality, safety, and environmental standards.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual serves as the foundational framework for ensuring consistency across all operational practices at our Corona, California facility. It defines standardized protocols to promote regulatory compliance, production excellence, and continuous improvement. This manual reinforces our belief that precision, responsibility, and collaboration drive excellence across every batch, every fill, and every customer interaction.
frontMatter.objective:
This SOP Manual has been developed to:
Establish a unified approach to key operational procedures.
Ensure compliance with local, federal, and international cosmetic regulations.
Promote operational efficiency while minimizing health, safety, and environmental risks.
Foster a culture of quality, responsibility, and sustainability.
Enable every team member to operate with clarity, purpose, and accountability.
frontMatter.scope: This manual applies to all internal departments, vendors, service providers, and partners associated with Arminak Solutions LLC dba KBL Cosmetics. It includes operations related to R&D, manufacturing, quality control, packaging, warehousing, maintenance, safety, and sustainability.

blocks.text: At Arminak Solutions LLC dba KBL Cosmetics, we recognize the potential impact of air pollutants and airborne particulates generated during manufacturing processes. This SOP is established to guide efforts in minimizing air emissions, managing indoor and outdoor air quality, and complying with all applicable air pollution control regulations at our Corona, California facility.

Minimize emissions from manufacturing and utility systems.
Ensure regulatory compliance with federal, state, and local air quality standards.
Protect employee health and nearby communities from airborne pollutants.
Implement emission control technologies and best practices.
Monitor air quality parameters and improve through continuous innovation.

blocks.text: Odor Management

Enclose all chemical mixing and formulation processes to contain volatile organic compounds (VOCs).
Use vapor balancing systems during chemical transfer to minimize odor release.
Install local exhaust ventilation near strong odor sources and maintain filters regularly.
Noise Control Measures

Install sound-absorbing wall panels and acoustic insulation in high-noise areas such as utility rooms and production floors.
Map noise levels across the facility on a bi-annual basis and assess against OSHA standards.
Provide hearing protection PPE to staff operating near high-decibel equipment and train them on proper usage.
Schedule maintenance during non-peak hours to reduce operational noise impact.

At Arminak Solutions LLC dba KBL Cosmetics, sustainability is deeply embedded in our commitment to responsible manufacturing. As a high-volume contract manufacturer and private-label partner for the personal care and cosmetic industry, we recognize the critical role we play in minimizing our environmental footprint. This SOP outlines our strategic framework for enhancing energy efficiency and reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions throughout our manufacturing facility in Corona, California. Our efforts align with our broader mission to integrate innovation, compliance, and sustainability in all operations.
The primary objectives of this SOP are to:

Standardize the monitoring, control, and optimization of energy usage.
Systematically reduce direct and indirect GHG emissions.
Comply with local, state, and federal environmental regulations.
Promote low-carbon operational practices and technology adoption.
Establish measurable performance indicators and tracking mechanisms.

This SOP applies to all Production lines, HVAC and utilities, Warehousing, Administrative and R&D areas operated by Arminak Solutions LLC dba KBL Cosmetics. It is applicable to equipment operators, facility managers, engineering personnel, maintenance teams, procurement departments, and third-party contractors engaged in energy-related activities.

rows.definition: GHG is acronym for Greenhouse Gases. These are gases that trap heat in the atmosphere, contributing to global warming. Key GHGs include carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and fluorinated gases.

CCS is acronym for Carbon Capture & Storage which is a technology designed to capture carbon dioxide emissions from industrial sources and store it underground to prevent it from entering the atmosphere.
CHP means Combined Heat & Power. It is a system that simultaneously generates usable heat and electricity from a single energy source, increasing overall efficiency.

VFD is acronym for Variable frequency Drive. It is an electronic device that controls the speed and torque of electric motors by varying input frequency and voltage, leading to significant energy savings.
Energy Management System - digital tools to track and optimize energy performance

body.text:

Document baseline performance of all high-energy-consuming assets.
Track historical usage data for trending and comparison.

Replace legacy systems with high-efficiency units.
Prioritize upgrades for high-consumption units based on audit outcomes.
Evaluate energy savings post-installation through EMS.

Introduce programmable logic controllers (PLCs) and automation.
Install motion sensors and timers in low-use areas.
Schedule batch production for optimized energy clustering.

Implement EMS to track real-time data across utilities.
Set usage thresholds with alerts for consumption anomalies.

At Arminak Solutions LLC dba KBL Cosmetics, maintaining a fair, inclusive, and compliant hiring process is essential to building a diverse and competent workforce. This SOP outlines structured procedures for recruiting, screening, and hiring employees in accordance with federal, state, and local labor laws, while upholding our commitments to equal opportunity, diversity, and internal growth.

To establish a standardized, transparent, and compliant recruitment process that ensures the selection of qualified candidates based on merit while promoting workplace diversity, ethical practices, and legal compliance.
This SOP applies to all recruitment and hiring activities for full-time, part-time, contract, and temporary positions across all departments and locations of Arminak Solutions LLC dba KBL Cosmetics.

rows.definition: A company that does not discriminate in hiring based on protected characteristics

responsibilities: Oversees recruitment strategy, compliance, and final offer approvals

body.text:
Hiring Manager submits job requisition form with justification.
HR reviews and approves the position in line with headcount planning.

Positions are posted internally and externally through the company portal and job boards.
All postings include clear qualifications and comply with Equal Opportunity principles.

Resumes are screened using standardized criteria focused on experience, skills, and role fit.
No decisions are made based on personal characteristics or demographic information.

Structured interviews are conducted with standardized questions for consistency.
Evaluation is based on pre-defined scoring rubrics.
Interview panels include diverse representation to reduce bias.

Selected candidates may undergo education, employment, and criminal background checks.
All checks comply with FCRA and privacy regulations.
Government-issued ID is required to confirm legal working age prior to onboarding.

HR prepares and issues offer letters.
Candidates complete onboarding and orientation programs.

blocks.text:
Employees are encouraged to apply for open roles through the internal career portal.
Internal mobility includes promotions, lateral transfers, and cross-functional assignments.
All internal applications are reviewed with equal consideration and confidentiality.
Participation in mentorship, leadership training, and development programs is encouraged.

This SOP shall be reviewed annually or whenever significant changes in labor laws or company recruitment policies occur. Any updates must be approved by the HR Director and communicated across all hiring teams.

This SOP outlines the procedure to safeguard third-party data from unauthorized access or disclosure and defines the methodology for gaining stakeholder consent, maintaining documentation, and ensuring data privacy and operational integrity.
Applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party vendors involved in handling, processing, or accessing third-party confidential data, including:

Physical and digital data security
Consent management processes
Stakeholder communications regarding data usage

rows.definition: Confidential information provided by external entities (clients, vendors, customers)

body.text:
Confidential printed documents must be stored in locked cabinets or controlled rooms.
Visitor access to data storage areas must be logged and monitored.

Implement role-based access controls to limit data visibility by role.
Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across all critical systems.
Encrypt sensitive data both at rest and during transmission.
Maintain detailed audit logs of all data access events and conduct periodic reviews.

A detailed Privacy Notice is provided before collecting any data, outlining:
Data categories collected
Purpose of data use
Information on third-party sharing (if applicable)
Retention period and data protection rights
Privacy Notices are accessible through:
Company website
Client onboarding materials
Contractual documentation

Explicit consent is collected using standardized Consent Forms.
Consents are stored digitally in a secure Consent Management System (CMS).
Records must be easily retrievable for audit and regulatory purposes.

Notify stakeholders of any significant changes to data processing policies.
Provide clear instructions on withdrawing consent and ensure requests are processed within 30 days.

narrative.text:

sops.title: Plan for Responding to Confidential Information Incidents

blocks.text: At Arminak Solutions LLC dba KBL Cosmetics, safeguarding confidential information is vital to our operations and reputation. This SOP outlines a structured incident response plan to detect, report, mitigate, and recover from any breach involving employee data, customer records, financial information, or proprietary data.

This SOP outlines the procedure for detecting, reporting, responding to, and mitigating any breach or unauthorized access involving confidential information. The aim is to ensure quick containment, minimal impact, and protection of stakeholder interests.

This Sop Applies to all departments, locations, systems, and personnel (internal or external) who handle or access confidential and sensitive information, including: Employee records , Customer/vendor data, Financial and legal information, Proprietary process, product or R&D information, Network/system security credentials

rows.definition: Non-public information impacting privacy, operations, or compliance

responsibilities: Coordinates IRP activation, investigation, and technical response

body.text:
All employees must report suspicious activity or confirmed breach within 1 hour.
Examples include unusual login alerts, unauthorized data transfer, lost devices, phishing attacks.

IT isolates affected systems/devices.
Access rights are revoked; firewalls updated.
Malware removed; evidence logs captured.

Identify type of data compromised (PII, business confidential, customer data).
Evaluate scope: number of records, systems affected, potential harm.

Notify affected internal stakeholders, regulatory bodies (if required), customers/vendors under legal guidance.
Communication is approved by Director – Information Security & Compliance Officer.

Restore systems from clean backups.
Change credentials across affected endpoints.
Monitor post-incident for anomalies.

Conducted by IT + Compliance within 3 working days.
Report includes timeline, actions taken, weaknesses exploited, corrective actions.

Internal debrief within 7 days.
Lessons learned applied to SOP updates, training programs, and IT policies.

blocks.text:
Quarterly training on phishing, data handling, and reporting channels.
Confidential data access is role-based (least privilege).
USBs and external media are restricted.
MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) enabled on cloud and email systems.
All incidents logged in the Information Security Incident Register, capturing:

Incident ID
Time of detection
Reported by
Systems affected
Type of data breached
Actions taken
Communication details
Lessons learned Retention Period: 7 Years
This SOP is reviewed annually or after major incidents.
